name: CT-04
label: Safe D

model.rationale: A strongly Democratic district, an incumbent with a roughly 90-to-1 cash advantage, and markets pricing the race near 97% Democratic all point the same direction. With no polling suggesting a competitive race, the forecast stays Safe Democratic with an expected margin around twenty points.
model.watch: A credible poll showing a single-digit race or a late wave of outside spending against Himes would be the main reason to revisit this rating.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.

overview:
Connecticut's 4th District leans heavily Democratic, with a partisan advantage of about 13 points, and Democrat Jim Himes has held the seat since 2009. He enters the general election with a large financial edge, holding roughly $2.4 million on hand after raising about $1.7 million. Republican Michael Goldstein has raised under $60,000 and reports about $25,000 available, while an independent candidate has raised only a few hundred dollars. No outside groups are spending in the race.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and markets. Prediction markets price Himes's chances around 97 percent. With a well-funded incumbent in a strongly Democratic district facing a minimally funded challenger, the seat is rated Safe Democratic, and the main uncertainty is the size of the winning margin rather than who wins.
